result: {"decisions":[{"point":"D2","problem":"How to measure unintended memorization when raw log-perplexity values depend heavily on model, application, and dataset.","did":"They inserted random canaries and measured a relative exposure metric comparing the canary's perplexity to that of equivalent non-inserted random sequences.","alternatives_named":["directly reporting the log-perplexity of the training data"],"stated_reason":"Raw log-perplexity is high or low depending on the specific model, application, or dataset, so it is ill suited as a direct measure of memorization.","quote":"Naively, we might try to measure a model’s unintended memorization of training data by directly reporting the log-perplexity of that data. However, whether the log-perplexity value is high or low depends heavily on the specific model, application, or dataset"},{"point":"D2","problem":"How to efficiently estimate exposure when the inserted canary has rank near 1 and random sampling rarely finds lower-perplexity candidates.","did":"They modeled the canary perplexity distribution with a skew-normal and extrapolated from it, checking the fit with a Kolmogorov–Smirnov test.","alternatives_named":["approximation by sampling","interpolation"],"stated_reason":"Sampling is inefficient when only very few alternate canaries have lower perplexity, since sampling distribution extremes is difficult.","quote":"However, this sampling method is inefficient if only very few alternate canaries have lower entropy than $s[r]$, in which case $|S|$ may have to be large to obtain an accurate estimate."},{"point":"D3","problem":"Whether the exposure metric actually corresponds to real extractability of memorized sequences.","did":"They built a shortest-path extraction algorithm and tested whether high exposure implies extraction across models trained to the same test accuracy, looking for false positives.","alternatives_named":["brute-force extraction"],"stated_reason":"The underlying hypothesis is that exposure is a useful measure for judging when canaries have been memorized, so they check there are not many false positives.","quote":"We now validate that when the exposure of a phrase is high, we can extract the phrase from the model (i.e., there are not many false positives, where exposure is high but we can’t extract it)."},{"point":"D2","problem":"Whether memorization detected with artificially inserted canaries is an artifact of the insertion.","did":"They ran the extraction analysis on the Enron email dataset, which contains naturally occurring secrets such as SSNs and credit card numbers.","alternatives_named":["experiments on data with artificially inserted canaries"],"stated_reason":"It is possible, though unlikely, that memorization is detected only because canaries were artificially inserted.","quote":"It is possible (although unlikely) that we detect memorization only because we have inserted our canaries artificially. To confirm this is not the case, we study a dataset that has many naturally-occurring secrets already in the training data."},{"point":"D1","problem":"Whether unintended memorization is merely a consequence of overtraining, which standard regularization would fix.","did":"They tested weight decay, dropout, and quantization, using a 5% PTB subset that overtrains so the regularizers could be assessed, and found none prevent memorization.","alternatives_named":["weight decay","dropout","quantization"],"stated_reason":"It might be reasonable to assume memorization stems from overtraining, so they test whether regularizers that prevent overtraining also prevent it.","quote":"In order to directly measure the effect of weight decay on a model that does overtrain, we take the first $5\\%$ of the PTB dataset and train our language model there."},{"point":"D2","problem":"How to compare memorization across training strategies when models differ in final accuracy.","did":"They controlled for final test accuracy by taking earlier checkpoints from better-performing models before comparing canary exposure.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"Not all optimizers converge to the same final test accuracy, so differences in exposure could be confounded with accuracy.","quote":"However, when we control for the final test accuracy by taking a checkpoint from an earlier epoch from those models that perform better, we found no statistically significant difference in the exposure of the canary"},{"point":"D4","problem":"Whether to continue pursuing automatic sanitization of training data via disagreement between two models as a defense.","did":"They dropped the approach after finding it missed secrets and was unsound, and judged sanitization not an effective defense on its own.","alternatives_named":["blacklist filtering","removing all numbers"],"stated_reason":"The approach missed some secrets and is unsound if the same secret is inserted twice; black-listing is never complete in security.","quote":"Unfortunately, this style of approach missed some secrets (and is unsound if the same secret is inserted twice)."},{"point":"D5","problem":"How to interpret exposure values near zero for DP models trained with very large, theoretically meaningless epsilon.","did":"They interpreted the negligible measured exposure as evidence that the analytic epsilon bound is loose, citing related work on the gap between empirical and theoretical privacy loss.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"Related studies found orders-of-magnitude gaps between measured privacy loss and the upper-bound epsilon, and improved proofs tighten guarantees without changing training.","quote":"Even with a vanishingly-small amount of noise, and values of $\\varepsilon$ that offer no meaningful theoretical guarantees, the measured exposure is negligible."},{"point":"D6","problem":"How strongly to claim the practical meaning of extraction time on Enron data.","did":"They cautioned that the local extraction time of a few hours should not be taken as the cost of a real attack.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"The local attack batches queries and does not include remote querying in the run-time computation.","quote":"Note that it would be unfair to draw from this that an actual attack would only take a few hours: this local attack can batch queries to the model and does not include any remote querying in the run-time computation."}]}
